props.title: Vice Versa
props.initialSlug: Father and son magically swap bodies in 80s comedy

sections.content: Vice Versa (1988) landed during the peak of body-swap comedies in the late 1980s, alongside Like Father Like Son (1987), 18 Again! (1988), and Big (1988). Judge Reinhold and Fred Savage capture the awkward hilarity of a father and son switching bodies through a magical Tibetan skull. The film taps into the era's fascination with parent-child role reversals, a theme that would continue through Freaky Friday (1976, remade 2003) and beyond. While not as commercially successful as Big, Vice Versa delivers sharp commentary on corporate culture and family dynamics.

sections.content: The body-swap genre peaked again in the early 2000s with 13 Going on 30 (2004) and 17 Again (2009) bringing fresh perspectives to the concept. These films expanded beyond simple parent-child switches to explore broader themes of aging, regret, and second chances. The Hot Chick (2002) took the premise into more outrageous territory, while The Change-Up (2011) brought an R-rated edge to the format.

Vice Versa particularly excels in its workplace scenes, where Savage (in Reinhold's body) must navigate corporate politics and adult relationships. This dynamic would later influence films like Little (2019), which specifically examined power dynamics in professional settings through its body-swap premise. The film's exploration of father-son relationships also laid groundwork for later family-focused switching films like The Family Man (2000). SUBHEAD: The Evolution of Body-Swap Cinema

movies.title: 17 Again

sections.content: The lasting influence of late-80s body-swap films like Vice Versa can be seen in modern variations like Your Name (2016) and Jumanji: Welcome to the Jungle (2017), which use consciousness-switching as a vehicle for both comedy and deeper themes. The genre continues to evolve with entries like Freaky (2020), which merged body-swapping with horror elements, proving the enduring versatility of the concept first popularized by films like Vice Versa.
